title: Forked integration case runners never run the leak check
description:
parallel_case_runner.h runs every case in a forked child that ends with _exit(), so LeakSanitizer never runs and ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=1 sanitizer runs of the scheduler and other suites report no leaks whatever happens. With an explicit __lsan_do_recoverable_leak_check() after each scheduler case, the only remaining report is the framework escape buffer, FND-20261113004147-cf2e-indigo-xml-escape-buffer-finding-001. Next: after that is fixed, run the leak check in the case runner child before _exit() where LeakSanitizer is available.

Imported from .factory/findings/active/FND-20261113001457-32cc-scheduler-shutdown-command-leak-001.json (category: quality, blocking: no).

outcome.summary: Pass. No concrete defect. Verified: (1) without sanitizer flags the preprocessed header differs from master only by 'int result = runner->child(...); _exit(result);'; (2) Apple clang 21 -fsanitize=address sets __has_feature(address_sanitizer) but not __SANITIZE_ADDRESS__; UBSan/TSan builds define neither, so they are unaffected; (3) the macOS ASan dylib (x86_64 and arm64 slices) exports ___lsan_do_recoverable_leak_check, a probe with a deliberate leak returns 0 on arm64 and on x86_64 under Rosetta, and detect_leaks=1 aborts with 'not supported on this platform' on both, so the AGENTS.md 'Apple Clang has no leak detector' holds for macOS; the shipped lsan_interface.h documents a 0 return when detection is disabled; (4) stub runner with -D__SANITIZE_ADDRESS__ and a check returning 1: the passing case prints 'Stub: leaks detected after passing' in its captured output followed by FAIL, the failing case is not checked; (5) make test-agent-scheduler 71/71; test_agent_scheduler_asan filtered case commands_queued_at_shutdown_are_released passes. False-positive risk under real LSan is low: all four suite parents are single-threaded at fork (no indigo_start before run_parallel_cases), so no allocations sit only on threads that are missing after fork; the scheduler child runs full cleanup() before returning; the archived ticket f91ea306 records a real LSan per-case run of the forked scheduler suite whose only report was the TLS escape buffer fixed in 48e10c044. Exposure is limited: the nexdome3 sanitize target forces detect_leaks=0, alpaca has no ASan build, only a manual Linux run of test_agent_scheduler_asan (detect_leaks defaults to 1 there) changes. Non-blocking doc nit: the AGENTS.md bullet implies detect_leaks=1 must be set, but on Linux it is the ASan default and the existing *-sanitize targets set detect_leaks=0, so they do not run the check. Out of scope: in nexdome3 --known-defects mode a leak would turn an UNEXPECTED PASS into EXPECTED FAIL (no make target combines

history.text: Verification on macOS arm64 (Apple clang 21, no Homebrew LLVM, no LSan): ordinary builds pass: test_agent_scheduler 71/71, test_dome_nexdome3_simulator 51/51, test_system_alpaca_simulator 277/277; omnisim suite skipped (needs external simulator). ASan build test_agent_scheduler_asan: Apple clang defines __has_feature(address_sanitizer) but not __SANITIZE_ADDRESS__; sanitizer/lsan_interface.h compiles and links, __lsan_do_recoverable_leak_check() returns 0, ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=1 aborts at startup (not supported on this platform), so the check is a no-op here. With detect_leaks=0 the ASan scheduler binary ran (filtered single case passes). Forced-path evidence: header compiled with -D__SANITIZE_ADDRESS__ and a stub lsan_interface.h whose check returns 1: the case fails with 'leaks detected after x' and the runner reports FAIL, exit 1. UNVERIFIED: real LeakSanitizer in the forked child (Linux/GCC/Linux clang) - false positives from parent-inherited state or threads absent after fork, and any real product leaks, could not be observed; no negative test with a real leak was possible. Windows: header is POSIX-only (fork, unistd.h) already, unaffected.
Check command-1 started: make -C indigo_test test-agent-scheduler
Checking sanitizer macros, preprocessed output and the ASan runtime symbol
Building scheduler suites (plain, ASan) and a forced-path stub runner in scratch
